question: Does the compact-orbit shared-factor-log DLP (normal-basis canonical probe, rank-guided relations, no pair table) beat frozen Kuhn-Struik batched signed-Frobenius rho at n=53 on identical published targets?

compact_ic.base: retained n=53 block_00 header (K=220) for panel 1; construct:53:0:<K> for panel 2

matching: batched rho generates the corpus; compact arm receives its published scalars; every fixture's published_q and recovered scalar must agree
decision_rule: compact arm overtakes at L only if all 3 block wall ratios compact/rho are < 1 (same rule as autolab_batched_rho_n53_20260922)

panel_1.order: block parity alternates which arm runs first

panel_2.K_rule: fit T(K) = a*K^2 + (K + L)*b/K^2 on the L=1024 sweep (K=220/440/660: a ~ 0.028 ms, b ~ 1.3e6 ms); pick the minimizer rounded to a multiple of 220
panel_2.order: block parity alternates which arm runs first

host_caveat: shared host; load average 30-50 from other sessions; load recorded per run; user CPU reported alongside wall
claim_boundary: Finite public-synthetic n=53 batches only. Both arms cost ~sqrt(L*r/n) at their optima, so this is a constant-factor comparison, not an asymptotic sub-rho claim. No key recovery, no external points, no deployed-curve claim.
